text:
maya: FYI we had a canary incident on dedicated-pool-3 where cloud preemptions coincided with a rapid scale-down and spiked routed traffic to hosted. Need a short-term config and a longer-term design for soft reserves and AZ-aware risk.

raj: Yeah saw the spike. Autoscaler pulled nodes fast (~8 nodes in <1m) on a transient dip. No hysteresis on scale-down.

oliver: Do we have telemetry showing whether the reclaim was cloud-initiated or our eviction path?

maya: Cloud reclaimed. But our admission policy left min_headroom=0 so there was zero buffer. Requests queued and then routed to hosted immediately.

ana: Would a small steady reserve help, or do we want a credit system to avoid constant cost?

raj: Cost vs reliability tradeoff. Prefer a credit-backed soft reserve: small baseline headroom + credits that can be used to prewarm when risk rises. Credits decay when unused.

oliver: Implementation: operator maintains "soft_headroom_credits" metric. Admission consumes credits before spinning new nodes. If credits exhausted, fall back to normal provisioning. Also need to separate "reserved slots" from burst admission so metrics and billing are clear.

maya: For an interim canary change I'm proposing:

```
min_headroom: 3
scale_down_grace: 300s
admission_window: 60s
fallback_debounce: 15s
burst_credit_window: 10m
```

raj: 3 GPUs min or 5% whichever is higher? For large pools, absolute 3 is too small.

maya: Right — adopt max(3, 5% of pool) as the canary rule.

oliver: And scale_down_grace 5m so we don't immediately dump KV caches on short dips. Also multiply backoff on repeated downsizes.

ana: Routing rule change: don't failover to hosted until a latency SLO breach persists for >15s and only after cross-AZ attempts. Immediate failover adds load to hosted and increases cost.

raj: Add an SLI for unexpected_hosted_fallbacks and an alert at >3/hour per pool. That will surface regressions fast.

maya: I'll PR the manifest + Prometheus rule. Will run the config for 24h and watch headroom utilization and fallback rate to hosted.

oliver: Long-term: operator should learn per-AZ preemption probability and maintain AZ-specific soft reserves. If an AZ has high reclaim risk, keep more local headroom there so cross-AZ routing is cheaper than hosted failover.

raj: We need telemetry: historical preemption/reclaim rate by AZ, time-of-day patterns, and correlation with price/spot signals. Feed that into a risk score and weight headroom.

ana: Also need finance/product sign-off for any policy that increases committed cost under Dedicated contracts. Flagging now.

maya: For canary we accept small cost delta. I'll sync with Product/Finance tomorrow. PR link when ready.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-342 created for canary fallback spike. Linked to thread 1715012345.

raj: Plan: deploy interim config to canary, monitor 24h, add SLI/alert, prototype credit model, and prototype AZ-risk model. Revert if >5 hosted fallbacks in 1h.

maya: Deploying now. Will report metrics after 2h and again at 24h. :thumbsup:

oliver: If we see noisy behavior, immediate rollback and short hotfix.

ana: I'll run queries against the preemption dataset to surface patterns by AZ/time.

maya: Thanks all — closing loop in PR when merged.
